options.distinctness: 7 courses differ each way (52.5 EC). Venture development, product design and market research distinguish this option from the first option’s emphasis on neurobiology, lifespan development and evidence synthesis.

analysis: Both plans retain eleven substantive biomedical courses including cellular biology, normal physiology, anatomy, lab work, immunity, pathology and drug mechanisms. They share statistics, data handling and general formation. The first extends the biological questions through comparative neurobiology, lifespan psychology and mental-health mechanisms and uses statistical learning, evidence synthesis and image processing. Machine Learning is taught with prediction, classification and validation on applied datasets, including medicine; it complements the basic data course, which precedes it. Image processing concerns computation, while anatomical imaging supports spatial reasoning. Neither supplies acquisition and instrumentation. The enterprise option uses seven distinct courses for venture planning, working prototypes, financial analysis, customer evidence, marketing and organisational strategy, anchored by the same biomedical science. Description-only Market Research and Strategy & Digital Transformation add actual enquiry and planning. They do not imply clinical product trials or biomedical regulatory study. Rhetoric in Action teaches coaching and public speaking with children, while the other rhetoric, language and creative courses cannot form a distinct biomedical teaching pathway. One candidate was therefore rejected on academic content. Shared rows are partial relationships of substantive courses, with the integrated 22 EC placement and defence separately visible.
